profile.reading:
Edged Chicago ORD01 is a wholesale/colocation data center campus built and operated by Edged (Edged Energy) at 2835 Bilter Road in Aurora, Illinois, within DuPage County, one of several purpose-built campuses the company markets under its Edged brand across North America. According to the company's own published materials, the Chicago campus sits on more than 65 acres and comprises two connected buildings, ORD01-1 and ORD01-2: a two-story, 24-megawatt building and a larger single-story, 72-megawatt building the company says can be further subdivided for individual tenants, together totaling roughly 96 megawatts of critical IT load across the campus.

Edged designs its facilities to a Tier III, concurrently maintainable standard and advertises a 100% uptime service-level agreement, backed by an on-site electrical substation sized for the campus's full build-out, N+1 uninterruptible power supply and generator redundancy (with generators specified using Tier 4 Final emissions-compliant engines), and revenue-grade real-time power metering, infrastructure typical of large wholesale data center developments aimed at hyperscale and enterprise tenants rather than small retail colocation customers. Each building is described as having two loading-dock bays, around-the-clock access, and two meet-me rooms connecting to multiple carrier-neutral fiber providers through four physically diverse points of entry.

Cooling is a notable feature of the design: Edged uses a proprietary waterless, closed-loop system it calls ThermalWorks, built around glycol heat transfer with N+1 redundancy, which the company states achieves a Water Usage Effectiveness of 0.00 liters per kilowatt-hour, eliminating the evaporative water consumption typical of conventional data center cooling towers, a design choice with particular relevance in a region where large industrial water draws have drawn public scrutiny. The company also states the system supports liquid-cooled racks at densities above 400 kilowatts each, well beyond what traditional air-cooled data halls can accommodate, positioning the campus for high-density AI and HPC workloads alongside conventional enterprise IT.

Fire protection includes a double-interlock, pre-action water-mist system in the data halls with addressable, hot-aisle-focused smoke detection, and the campus is secured with perimeter fencing, biometric access control, and CCTV. Edged reports a projected mechanical PUE of 1.086 for the Chicago site and an estimated six-nines (99.9999%) availability figure. Individual tenants and per-building square footage have not been published by the company.

profile.research_note: Edged's own Chicago page states 96MW total across the campus' two buildings: ORD01-1 (24MW, two-story) and ORD01-2 (72MW, single-story, splittable). Campus sits on 65+ acres at 2835 Bilter Rd, Aurora IL; individual building sqft not published. Tier III design, concurrently maintainable, 100% uptime SLA claimed.

reading.body:
This facility is Edged's first completed US building on a planned three-building campus in Aurora, Illinois, near Chicago's O'Hare airport. The operator published a 96 megawatt capacity for ORD01 at opening in February 2025, though some third-party sources initially listed 48 megawatts, a gap the operator attributes to phased delivery. At an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack for AI training workloads, 96 megawatts of IT load represents roughly 2,400 racks, a scale typical of purpose-built hyperscale AI facilities rather than traditional colocation campuses.

The facility uses waterless cooling with a reported power usage effectiveness of 1.15, a metric that qualifies it for power-constrained deployments where cooling infrastructure matters as much as electricity supply. The campus location in Illinois places it outside the handful of states where published megawatt figures exist in public operator specs, and ORD01 ranks seventh among only six Illinois facilities with published capacity data, reflecting how little capacity is formally declared in the state despite 44 mapped data center sites.

Edged announced three buildings planned for this Aurora campus, but only ORD01's opening is published. The second and third phases remain unannounced in the operator's public materials, meaning total eventual campus size cannot be determined from the facts available. The facility matters to AI scaling primarily as a proof point that new hyperscale-focused developers are delivering power-dense buildings where the grid can supply them, rather than as a standalone constraint on national AI capacity.
